VA-S.note: AP called the race for Warner; Fox 5 DC published the call at 7:03 p.m. ET and WDBJ7 at 7:13 p.m. No statewide count was readable from this run.

GA-S.src: NBC News count (via GV Wire); AP call via Fox 5 Atlanta
GA-S.note: AP called the race for Ossoff at 7:55 p.m. ET (per Fox 5 Atlanta; AP's own 'Ossoff wins reelection' story followed in the feed at 8:07 p.m.). Count shown is NBC News's at 7:37 p.m. (25% of expected); no newer statewide count was readable from the 8:40 p.m. run.

SC-S.src: NBC News count (via GV Wire, 10:03 p.m.); AP call via AP story in the news feed (12:46 a.m. ET)
SC-S.note: AP's story 'Democrat Annie Andrews wins US Senate election in South Carolina over Republican Darline Graham' appeared in the feed at 12:46 a.m. ET; AP's 1:30 a.m. balance-of-power story lists South Carolina among AP-called flips. Count shown is NBC News's at 10:03 p.m. (86% in); no newer count readable.

SC-G.note: Early returns reflecting a small share of the vote; AP had not called the race as of 7:23 p.m. ET.

IL-S.note: AP's story 'Democrat Juliana Stratton wins election to U.S. Senate from Illinois' appeared in the feed at 8:01 p.m. ET; no statewide count was readable from this run.

TX-S.src: AP count via Texas Tribune (9:35 p.m. ET); AP call via TIME
TX-S.note: AP called the race for Talarico 'late Tuesday' (TIME, published 11:04 p.m. ET; exact call time not verified). Count is AP's at 9:35 p.m. ET (52% of expected vote); NBC's later projection (63.5% counted) showed Talarico 59.4%, Paxton 39.1%, Brown 1.5% (GV Wire) but no newer raw totals were readable.

KY-S.note: AP called the race for Barr; WKYT published the call at 9:15 p.m. ET (AP's call may have come earlier). With 71% of the statewide vote counted Barr had 53%, Booker 44%; no raw totals were readable.

NC-S.note: AP projected Cooper the winner; WLOS published the call at 8:26 p.m. ET and PBS NewsHour's live blog carried it at 8:47 p.m. No statewide count was readable from this run.

CO-S.note: AP called the race for Hickenlooper at poll close (9 p.m. ET), per GV Wire; no count was readable.

NM-S.note: AP called the race for Luján right after polls closed (9 p.m. ET), before any votes were reported, per GV Wire.

WY-S.note: AP called the open seat for Hageman at poll close (9 p.m. ET), per GV Wire; no count was readable.

MA-G.note: AP called the race for Healey at 8:01 p.m. ET, one minute after polls closed (State House News Service); no count was readable.

IL-G.note: AP called the race for Pritzker minutes after polls closed at 8 p.m. ET (Shaw Local headline; exact minute not verified); no count was readable.

PA-G.note: AP projected Shapiro the winner (Bloomberg headline, seen 9:50 p.m. ET; the call itself came earlier, The Hill reported it at 8:23 p.m.); call time not verified. No count was readable.

NY-G.note: AP projected Hochul the winner over Blakeman (Bloomberg and Fox 5 NY headlines, seen 9:50 p.m. ET; polls closed 9 p.m.); exact call time not verified. No count was readable.

GA-G.note: PBS NewsHour's AP-powered results page is headlined 'Keisha Lance Bottoms wins Governor race in Georgia' (seen 9:50 p.m. ET; NBC and MultiState also show Bottoms as winner); exact AP call time not verified. No statewide count was readable.

OH-S.note: AP called the special election for Brown at 11:10 p.m. ET (GV Wire: 8:10 p.m. Pacific); count is AP's as published by GV Wire at 11:13 p.m. ET with an estimated 87% counted.

OH-G.src: Cincinnati Enquirer percentages (10 p.m.); AP call via Ohio Capital Journal ('the Associated Press projects') and AP's own story
OH-G.note: Ohio Capital Journal reported the AP projection at 10:49 p.m. ET; AP's story 'Democrat Amy Acton defeats Vivek Ramaswamy' appeared in the feed at 1:07 a.m. Percentages shown are the Enquirer's 10 p.m. entry (72% in); no raw totals readable.

CA-G.src: AP and NBC News (via GV Wire)
CA-G.note: NBC News and AP projected Becerra the winner over Hilton shortly after polls closed at 11 p.m. ET (GV Wire, published 11:05 p.m. ET); no count was readable.

AR-S.src: AP and NBC News (via GV Wire)
AR-S.note: NBC News projected Cotton's reelection and AP also called it (GV Wire, published 10:47 p.m. ET; exact call time not verified; polls closed 8:30 p.m.). No count was readable.

DE-S.note: AP called the race for Coons as polls closed at 8 p.m. ET (GV Wire, published 8:06 p.m. ET); no count was readable.

MA-S.note: AP called the race for Markey at the 8 p.m. ET poll close, before any votes were reported (GV Wire, published 8:06 p.m. ET); no count was readable.

NJ-S.note: AP called the race for Booker as polls closed at 8 p.m. ET (GV Wire, published 8:06 p.m. ET); no count was readable.

RI-S.note: AP called the race for Reed as polls closed at 8 p.m. ET (GV Wire, published 8:06 p.m. ET); no count was readable.

FL-S.src: NBC News count (via GV Wire); AP call via AP story (Fox Carolina)
FL-S.note: AP: 'The Associated Press declared Moody the winner at 8:34 p.m. EST.' Count shown is NBC News's via GV Wire (8:36 p.m., 95.5% of expected).

KS-S.src: NBC News count (via GV Wire); AP call via AP story (Yahoo News)
KS-S.note: AP: 'The Associated Press declared Hamilton the winner at 11:24 p.m. EST.' Count shown is NBC News's via GV Wire (11:22 p.m.); share counted not stated.

IA-S.src: AP call via Iowa Capital Dispatch (Yahoo); NBC News count (via GV Wire)
IA-S.note: AP projected Turek the winner over Hinson (Iowa Capital Dispatch, published 11:51 p.m. ET; exact call time not verified): Turek nearly 51%, Hinson 46%, Laehn just over 3% with 92% of precincts reporting. The 89.5% figure is NBC's earlier expected-vote estimate; no raw totals were readable.

NH-S.src: AP (AP story 'Chris Pappas defeats John E. Sununu' in the news feed, 12:10 a.m. ET)
NH-S.note: AP's own story declaring Pappas the winner appeared in the feed at 12:10 a.m. ET; AP's 1:30 a.m. balance-of-power story lists New Hampshire among AP-called races. NBC News had projected Pappas earlier. No statewide count readable from this run.

AL-S.src: AP (AP story via Yahoo News, Houston Chronicle)
AL-S.note: AP: 'The Associated Press declared Moore the winner at 11:17 p.m. EST.' No statewide count readable from this run.

TN-S.note: NBC News projected Hagerty the winner (GV Wire, published 9:56 p.m. ET); no count readable. An AP call was not confirmed by this run, so the desk shows no call.

OK-S.src: NBC News (via GV Wire); The Hill
OK-S.note: NBC News projected Hern the winner (GV Wire, published 9:56 p.m. ET; The Hill carried the result at 8:05 p.m.); no count readable. An AP call was not confirmed by this run, so the desk shows no call.

TX-G.src: AP (AP story in the news feed, 12:28 a.m. ET)
TX-G.note: AP's story 'Democrat Gina Hinojosa elected Texas' first Latina governor, ousts Republican incumbent Greg Abbott' appeared in the feed at 12:28 a.m. ET (US media had projected it from 11:19 p.m.). No statewide count readable.

MN-S.note: AP declared Flanagan the winner at 12:07 a.m. EST (AP story carried by Northern News Now, published 12:35 a.m. ET); no count was readable.

ME-S.src: AP (AP story via PBS NewsHour, Boston 25 News; AP balance-of-power story 1:30 a.m. lists Maine among AP-called flips)
ME-S.note: AP's story 'Troy Jackson wins the Maine US Senate race over GOP Sen. Susan Collins' was published at 1:06 a.m. ET; AP's 1:30 a.m. balance-of-power story counts Maine among seven Senate flips called by AP. Collins conceded about 12:30 a.m. No statewide count was readable from this run.

WI-G.src: AP (via PBS NewsHour results page headline)
WI-G.note: PBS NewsHour's AP-powered results page is headlined 'David Crowley wins Governor election in Wisconsin' (seen 12:50 a.m. ET; the call itself came earlier, exact time not verified; WKOW and WSAW also report Crowley the winner). No count was readable.

MI-G.src: AP (AP story via Yahoo News; WXYZ 'AP projects')
MI-G.note: AP: 'The Associated Press declared Benson the winner at 1:45 a.m. EST.' No statewide count readable from this run.

AZ-G.src: AP (AP story via Yahoo News; ABC15 'AP reports')
AZ-G.note: AP: 'The Associated Press declared Hobbs the winner at 3:20 a.m. EST.' CBS News had projected it earlier. No statewide count readable from this run.

MI-S.src: NBC News count (via GV Wire); AP call via GV Wire
MI-S.note: GV Wire's 11:27 p.m. ET update: 'The Associated Press called the race for El-Sayed.' Count is NBC News's as published by GV Wire about 1:36 a.m. ET (about 77.6% of expected, roughly 1.1 million votes remaining).

NE-S.note: AP: 'The Associated Press declared Ricketts the winner at 3:27 a.m. EST.' Ricketts had claimed victory earlier with the count still under way (Nebraska Examiner). No statewide count readable from this run.

LA-S.note: AP: 'The Associated Press declared Letlow the winner at 12:31 a.m. EST.' No statewide count readable from this run.

AK-S.src: Alaska Division of Elections results via The Alaska Current
AK-S.note: Second batch of results, about 27% counted (The Alaska Current, updated about 10:14 p.m. AKST): Peltola 48.11%, Dan S. Sullivan 47.96%, Heikes 1.99%, Dan J. Sullivan 1.64%. Raw totals not shown. Too close to call; tens of thousands of absentee ballots remain (15-day window), ranked-choice tabulation Nov. 18 if no one tops 50%.

AK-G.src: Alaska Division of Elections results via The Alaska Current
AK-G.note: About 27% counted (The Alaska Current, updated about 10:14 p.m. AKST): Kreiss-Tomkins 49.73%, Wilson 28.91%, Bronson 13.93%, Taylor 7.15%. Raw totals not shown; not called. Ranked-choice tabulation Nov. 18 if no one tops 50%.

IA-G.src: AP (via Iowa Capital Dispatch 'AP projects'; AP's own story 1:00 a.m. ET)
IA-G.note: Iowa Capital Dispatch carried the AP projection at 11:17 p.m. ET; AP's story 'Democrat Rob Sand wins election to be Iowa's next governor' appeared in the feed at 1:00 a.m. No statewide count readable.

FL-G.src: AP (AP story in the news feed, 11:01 p.m. ET)
FL-G.note: AP's story 'Republican Byron Donalds is elected Florida's first Black governor' appeared in the feed at 11:01 p.m. ET. No statewide count readable.

MN-G.src: AP (AP story via WFSB / Gray TV, 12:17 a.m. ET)
MN-G.note: AP's story 'Amy Klobuchar Elected Minnesota Governor, Defeating Republican Lisa Demuth' was published by Gray TV stations at 12:17 a.m. ET; NBC and CBS projected it about the same time. No statewide count readable.

AL-G.note: AP: 'The Associated Press declared Tuberville the winner at 1:36 a.m. EST.' No statewide count readable from this run.
